events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the driver, so the fee can only stand through NS-1 [F3][NS-0]. NS-1 (i) is satisfied: the record shows a tap on "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 [F5][NS-1]. The location limb fails: at that moment the driver was 613 m from the pickup point, his closest approach over the whole episode was 612 m at 08:15:30, and he never came within 200 m [F1][F5][NS-1]. The wait limb also fails: after the tap he spent 0 s inside the pickup radius, and his 6 min 20 s stationary period was served 613 m away [F2][F5][NS-1]. The platform's own record agrees — driver_arrived_at is null [F4][NS-1].

Because NS-1 (ii) and (iii) are not met, the $6.61 charged at the 08:19:30 cancellation is not valid and must be returned in full [F3][F6][NS-2]. The amount is the cancellation fee exactly as recorded, with no surge component (1.0×), $6.61 [F6][F7][NS-2], payable as a voucher under NS-7.

The driver's written explanation — that Victoria Street was "too jammed to get closer" [F13] — is a statement, and the traffic record contradicts it: Victoria Street ran at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) during 08:00–08:30 and no incident was recorded near the route [F14][F16][NS-2]. System records override statements, and the congestion excuse would not in any event satisfy the GPS location test [F1][F13][F14][NS-1]. His chat message "I'm here already, please come out" at 08:16 [F9] is likewise contradicted by the GPS placing him 613 m away at that instant [F5][NS-1].

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the tap), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.
Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup > 3 min after the tap, until cancelling), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach to Bugis Junction (Victoria St entrance) was 612 m and he never came within 200 m (F1), and the GPS shows he sat stationary at (1.2958, 103.8495) — 613 m from the pickup — for 6 min 20 s from 08:13:10 to 08:19:30 (F2).

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 while 613 m from the pickup point and then stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds, so NS-1 (ii) is not satisfied (F5); the platform likewise never recorded a driver arrival (driver_arrived_at is null, F4).
Because NS-1 (ii) fails, the $6.61 cancellation fee charged on 08:19:30 when the driver cancelled as a no-show is not valid and must be refunded in full (F3, F6).

The driver's written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes" and that "Victoria Street was too jammed to get closer" (F13) is contradicted by the system record: he waited at a point 613 m away, and Victoria Street was running at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) with no incidents recorded during the trip window (F1, F2, F14, F16).

The rider did everything required of her: she messaged at 08:14 that she was waiting at the Victoria St entrance (F8), asked again at 08:17 that she saw no car and asked for the plate (F10), and the chat record is complete with all four messages timestamped (F12), so there is no evidence she failed to show up.

The driver pressing "I'm Here" while GPS places him outside the pickup area is the abuse-of-cancellation/waiting-button pattern, and he already has 2 no-show disputes upheld in the last 90 days (F19), so the account should be referred to Ryde for review alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The rider's own messages do not state her exact live location beyond "the Victoria St entrance" (F8, F10), and there is no rider-side GPS fact confirming she was at the pickup point during 08:13–08:19.
The driver did wait a genuine 6 min 20 s in the vicinity (F2) and did attempt contact (F9), so the driver may argue he made a real effort and that 613 m was the closest the traffic allowed (F13).
The chat shows the rider asked for the plate at 08:17 (F10) but no message of hers after the driver announced cancellation at 08:19 (F11), which the driver may spin as her going quiet.

claims.assertion: The rider did initiate contact and was present: her own chat message at 08:14 asks the driver where he is because she is waiting at the Victoria St entrance of Bugis Junction (F8), so there is no basis for treating her as a rider who never intended to show.

The driver did press "I'm Here", so limb (i) of NS-1 is satisfied on the system record: F5 shows the tap at 08:16:00, and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped so nothing is missing from the message history (F12).

The 3-minute wait limb of NS-1 is met on elapsed time: acceptance was at 08:10:05 and cancellation at 08:19:30, and the driver was stationary from 08:13:10 to 08:19:30, i.e. well over three minutes before cancelling (F2, F3).

The driver's explanation for pressing the button off-site is that Victoria Street was too jammed to get closer (F13), and the traffic record shows Victoria Street running at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) with no incidents in the trip window (F14, F16); this does not satisfy the location requirement of NS-1 (ii), which is measured against GPS rather than against congestion.

Because the location element is not made out on the system record — the closest approach was 612 m at 08:15:30 and the driver never came within 200 m, with driver_arrived_at null — the cancellation fee cannot stand under NS-1 and the correct disposition is to return the $6.61 already charged (F1, F4, F6).
The return should be made as a full refund of the cancellation fee of $6.61, computed from the fare record showing exactly that sum charged (F6, F7), in the voucher form required for such refunds.

No account flag should attach to the driver on this record: the "I'm Here" tap was made at 08:16:00 while stationary (F5, F2), i.e. he was not triggering a fee while parked elsewhere, and his 90-day history shows 540 trips with only 2 no-show disputes (F19).

weaknesses: The other side will rely on F1 (closest approach 612 m, never within 200 m), F2 (stationary 613 m from pickup) and F4 (driver_arrived_at null) to show the driver was nowhere near the Victoria St entrance — this defeats the NS-1 (ii) requirement and is the strongest fact set in the case.

The driver's own chat message "I'm here already, please come out" at 08:16 (F9) is contradicted by F5, which places him 613 m away at that exact moment, so the system record beats the statement and makes the event look misleading to the rider.

F13 ("Victoria Street was too jammed to get closer") is only a written statement and is undercut by F14, which records Victoria Street at 40–49 km/h band 5 — not congestion — and by F16 showing no incidents; it cannot excuse the location failure under NS-1/NS-2.
F19 shows 2 upheld no-show disputes against this driver in 90 days, so the other side can argue a pattern even though no flag is requested here.

points.response: Conceded — the rider's 08:14 message (F8) is on-record presence that supports our C5; it confirms she was at the Victoria St entrance while the driver was not.

Limb (i) is satisfied (F5 records the tap at 08:16:00), but the same fact defeats the driver: the tap was made 613 m from the pickup with 0 s spent within 200 m, and the platform never recorded an arrival (F4), so NS-1 (ii) fails.

Elapsed time alone cannot satisfy NS-1: the wait must be served at the pickup point, and F2 puts the entire 6 min 20 s stationary period at 613 m from the pickup, with a closest approach of 612 m (F1).

Agreed and adopted: NS-1 (ii) is measured against GPS, not congestion, and the excuse fails on its own terms because Victoria Street ran at band 5, 40–49 km/h, with no incidents and fair weather (F13, F14, F16, F17).
Conceded — F1, F4 and F6 are dispositive and the driver's own brief agrees with our C3 that the $6.61 cannot stand under NS-1.
Conceded on amount and form: $6.61 is the sum on the fare record (F6) with no surge (F7), payable as a Ryde voucher under NS-7; we ask refund_full of $6.61.

We do not ask the flag to decide the case, but it stands as an additional action: the driver told the rider "I'm here already" at 08:16 (F9) while F5 places him 613 m away with 0 s inside 200 m, and F19 shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days against a rider with 0 (F18).

Conceded on the core measurement: the GPS record does show the closest approach was 612 m at 08:15:30 with the vehicle never inside 200 m (F1) and stationary 613 m away from 08:13:10 to 08:19:30 (F2). This is the element that decides the case against the fee, and the driver does not contest it.
Conceded: the "I'm Here" tap at 08:16:00 was made 613 m from the pickup point with 0 s spent within 200 m afterwards (F5), and no driver arrival was ever recorded (F4), so NS-1 (ii) is not satisfied.

Agreed, and this is also the driver's own requested outcome: because NS-1 (ii) fails, the $6.61 charged on the 08:19:30 cancellation (F3, F6) is not valid and should be returned in full under NS-2 / NS-7, which matches the driver's claim D5/D6.

Accepted that F13 does not carry the driver home: the traffic record shows Victoria Street at speed band 5, 40–49 km/h during 08:00–08:30 (F14), with no incidents in the trip window (F16), so the "too jammed to get closer" explanation is not corroborated by traffic evidence.

Accepted; the complete, fully timestamped four-message record (F12) containing her 08:14 and 08:17 messages (F8, F10) shows the rider was actively waiting and asking for the vehicle, and no fact shows a rider no-show.

Contested as to the flag: the rider cites RD-6, which by its terms applies only where route-deviation liability is established, and the button-abuse consequence in NS-2 attaches only when the driver pressed "I'm Here" while showing as outside the pickup point as a deliberate fee-triggering device — here he pressed it at 08:16:00 while already stationary since 08:13:10 (F2, F5) and then cancelled rather than collecting the $6.61 (F3, F6), and the 2 upheld disputes in F19 are the same two no-show entries already being resolved by this refund, so a referral would double-count a single course of conduct rather than show a pattern of abuse.
